advisor_identified: Richard C. Hoffmann, historian of medieval Europe and environmental history, professor emeritus at York University.

doctorate.title: Studies in the Rural Economy of the Duchy of Wroclaw, 1200-1530

evidence.says: York University repository metadata identifies Hoffmann, Richard C. as advisor of Dagomar Degroot’s The Frigid Golden Age: Experiencing Climate Change in the Dutch Republic, 1560-1720, a History PhD dissertation with a 2014 copyright date.

York’s faculty profile identifies Richard C. Hoffmann as professor emeritus in History, with interests in environmental history and premodern Europe, and lists a PhD in Medieval Studies from Yale University.
York’s Richard Hoffmann fonds biography states that Richard C. Hoffmann received his PhD in Medieval Studies from Yale University in 1970 and joined York’s Department of History in 1971.

Yale’s Department of History dissertation list places Hoffman, Richard under 1970 with Studies in the Rural Economy of the Duchy of Wroclaw, 1200-1530, exactly matching the linked dissertation’s title and year.

notes: The linked record matches his Yale doctorate and dissertation. Yale’s list spells the surname Hoffman; York uses Hoffmann. York describes the degree as Medieval Studies, while the dissertation appears in Yale’s History list, consistent with the AHA department label.
